findings.title: Gate validator accepts a review whose invocation_reference points at an unrelated run of the same role (e.g. the T-DG0-LOAD load check)
findings.reproduction: QA_REPO_ROOT=<repo> node --test docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/tests/dg0-gate-negative.test.mjs --test-name-pattern QA-N27. The fixture builds a valid DG0 gate, then adds a second, successful qa-verifier run whose meta.json has task T-DG0-LOAD, assignment docs/delivery/assignments/DG0/T-DG0-LOAD.md and started_at before the candidate froze. It then points the qa-verifier review record's invocation_reference at that run. validateGate() returns no errors. In the real repository, successful LOAD runs exist for all four review roles (docs/delivery/runs/DG0/DG0-T-DG0-LOAD-{domain-reviewer,code-security-reviewer,qa-verifier,release-auditor}-*), so a complete DG0 gate could validate with no review invocation ever having run. checkInvocation() in tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs compares only role, session_id and exit status.
findings.expected: The validator (A24: rejects missing or invalid evidence; A23: separate actual review evidence) rejects a review or audit record whose run is not bound to it: the run's meta.assignment/task must match the record's assignment/review task, and the run must start after the candidate froze (meta.started_at >= stage candidate.frozen_at, or meta.head_commit_at_start containing the frozen commit). A regression test must cover this.
findings.actual: The validator accepts the record. validateGate returns [] (test QA-N27 fails with 'validator accepted an invalid gate (no errors)'). The meta.json fields that would bind a run to a review (task, assignment, assignment_sha256, started_at, head_commit_at_start) are recorded but never checked.

findings.title: Register evidence entries without a '/' are never existence-checked, so a bare non-existent file name satisfies an IMPLEMENTED row
findings.reproduction: QA_REPO_ROOT=<repo> node --test docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/tests/dg0-gate-negative.test.mjs --test-name-pattern QA-N28. It sets REQ-DLV-001 (final_gate DG0, IMPLEMENTED) evidence to 'NO-SUCH-EVIDENCE.md'. checkRegister() reports no error because rules.mjs only checks paths where ev.includes('/'). Real rows REQ-DLV-002 and REQ-DLV-019 cite 'CLAUDE.md', which exists but is checked only by luck.
findings.expected: requirements-spec.md: 'every row with final_gate <= DGn is IMPLEMENTED with non-empty evidence, and every evidence path exists'. Either every evidence entry that isn't an explicit test-ID token (for example a defined prefix such as 'test:') is existence-checked, or the spec defines the test-ID syntax that is exempt.
findings.actual: A bare file name is silently treated as a non-path token and accepted. I would accept this as a Low observation if it is tracked, but I recommend fixing it together with F-DG0-201.

findings.title: Stage plan puts acceptance-test authorship for A01-A22 in P6, but acceptance-map requires A03-A05 and A08-A11 to pass at DG4 and A02, A06, A07, A15 and A16 at DG5
findings.reproduction: Read docs/analysis/stage-plan.md line 122 (P6: 'qa-verifier authors A01–A22 tests under tests/qa/** and e2e/**') and compare it with docs/analysis/acceptance-map.md rows A02-A16 ('Must pass at' DG4/DG5). Sections P2-P5 of the stage plan name no owner for the executable REQ-S20-00x acceptance tests that must pass at those gates.
findings.expected: Every scenario has a concrete owner and stage for its executable test, consistent with the gate at which it must pass. For example, the stage plan says that the executable A-tests for DG2-DG5 are authored in P2-P5 (by the implementers, or by qa-verifier test-first before freeze), and that P6 extends and re-runs them.
findings.actual: The acceptance map is internally consistent: every scenario has a test level, a first-delivered stage and a gate (independent check 14-acceptance-feasibility.log, 0 errors). The stage plan's only authorship statement is in P6, which reads as later than the gates it must serve. This is feasible but ambiguous. I would accept it as a Low observation.
